Against the run it allows a 49.8% success rate [dc4] over 303 run plays [dc5], with an average of 6.5 defenders in the box [dc6]. CLE's ground game has been inefficient at -0.14 EPA per run [dc7] over 214 carries [dc8], so the box count is not light enough to guarantee room; CLE needs blocking wins rather than numbers. On passing, LV allows a 51.6% success rate [dc9]. CLE's pass offense produces explosives on 8.8% of pass plays [dc10], while LV allows explosives on 11.1% of plays [dc11], which favors CLE on the deep ball. LV's pressure proxy is 16.0% [dc12] of 374 dropbacks [dc13], and it sends five or more rushers on 28.6% of dropbacks [dc14] with 4.3 rushers on average [dc15]; expect fire-zone pressure and plan quick, hot throws on early downs. In the red zone LV allows touchdowns on 71.1% of drives [dc16] over 45 drives [dc17], 30th in the league [dc18], and it allows third-down conversions on 47.3% [dc19] over 129 attempts [dc20], also 30th [dc21]. The red-zone sample is small, but CLE should be aggressive on third and short and cash trips inside the 20.
